Architecture

Abbreviations used on this page (TSDB, WAL, TTL, HWM, XPUB, ZMQ, SQLite, JSON, CLI, API, RSS, fd, PEP, CORS, OBS...) are defined in the Abbreviations & jargon section.

System overview

                  ┌───────────────────────────────  sqtseries  ───────────────────────────────┐
 Producer ─PUSH───►│ PULL 12501 ──► validate ──► store.insert_many ──► SQLite (WAL, monthly     │
                   │                                        │               partitions)          │
                   │                                        └──► PUB 12503 ────► Subscriber      │
 QueryClient ◄─REQ─│ REP 12502 ◄── TimeSeriesDB ◄───────────┘                                   │
 Admin     ◄─REQ── │ REP 12504 ◄── ping/health/stats/optimize/backup/vacuum/connections         │
 Browser   ◄─HTTP─►│ FastAPI 12505 ──► TimeSeriesDB + PubSub (direct, no ZMQ hop)               │
 Monitor   ◄─SUB── │ PUB 12506 ── conn / sub / report events (every 10s)                        │
                   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

sqtseries is one process, one event loop, one SQLite file. The HTTP gateway (FastAPI served in-process by uvicorn on port 12505) talks directly to the engine and the PubSub bus; there is no ZMQ hop for HTTP traffic.

The rest of this page is for maintainers and anyone curious how things are put together. Regular users do not need it.

Ports and protocols

Ports default to 12501–12506 (configurable in Configuration). The only port that is auto-detected is the ingest port: with [ports] auto_detect = true (the default) it is the first free port in 12500–12700 — usually 12500, not the configured 12501 — while the other five ports (query/stream/admin/http/stats) always use their configured values.

ProtocolPortDataHWM
PUSH → PULL12501Ingestion (one measurement per frame, JSON)101,000
REQ/REP12502Query / aggregate requests1,000
XPUB/SUB12503Live measurements (topic = metric)10,000
REQ/REP12504Admin commands (ping/health/stats/optimize/backup/vacuum/connections/conncheck/subscribers)1,000
HTTP + WebSocket12505REST (/api/v1/*) + /ws/subscribe — direct engine access, no ZMQn/a (rate-limited)
PUB12506Stats events (conn, sub, report every 10 s)1,000

Components

SQLite engine

Raw sqlite3 layer (engine/): WAL pragmas, BEGIN IMMEDIATE writer transactions, executemany inserts, monthly partitions, VACUUM INTO backups.

Query engine

query/: raw fetches, Python aggregation/downsampling, and the rollup fast path (eligible queries only).

Messaging

messaging/: PULL ingest, REP query + admin, XPUB live bus, stats PUB, connection registry (with health sweep for stale detection), query result cache (LRU with TTL), worker pool.

HTTP gateway

FastAPI REST + WebSocket (gateway/), rate-limited (600 req/min), CORS-enabled.

Background tasks

Rollup (hourly pre-aggregates), retention (partition drops), maintenance (ANALYZE), backup (scheduled snapshots), WAL checkpointing.

Service

service.py: startup sequence, runtime file, graceful shutdown (PRAGMA optimize + checkpoint of the WAL).

SQLite schema

Tables are created by engine/schema.py; measurements live in monthly partitions named measurements_YYYY_MM.

-- Series identity: metric + JSON tags -> integer id
CREATE TABLE series (
    series_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    metric TEXT NOT NULL,
    tags TEXT,                      -- JSON-encoded TEXT (not SQLite JSON type)
    CONSTRAINT ck_tags_json CHECK (tags IS NULL OR json_valid(tags))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_series_metric_tags ON series(metric, tags);

-- Measurements: monthly partitions, WITHOUT ROWID = clustered PK
CREATE TABLE measurements_YYYY_MM (
    series_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- nanosecond epoch
    value REAL NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (series_id, timestamp_ns)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX ix_measurements_YYYY_MM_ts ON measurements_YYYY_MM(timestamp_ns);

-- Hourly rollup (count/sum/min/max so avg is derived) + watermark table
CREATE TABLE rollup_hourly (
    series_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    hour_start_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    count INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sum REAL NOT NULL,
    min REAL NOT NULL,
    max REAL NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (series_id, hour_start_ns)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE rollup_meta (
    k TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    v INTEGER NOT NULL
);

The timestamp_ns secondary index serves cross-series range queries and retention; per-series ranges use the clustered primary key (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: SEARCH … USING PRIMARY KEY).

Write path

Ingestion is serialized by SQLite itself — a receive-only drain loop hands parsed batches through a bounded hand-off queue (at most ingestion.pending_max batches outstanding, enforced by a semaphore) to a dedicated persister task; batching happens at the drain step:

  1. PUSH frames arrive on port 12501 (HWM 101,000; when the bounded queue fills, the drain loop suspends and the producer blocks at its own send buffer — backpressure, never silent loss).
  2. The worker step drains up to 1024 frames per tick (NOBLOCK) and validates each: orjson decode, then parse_ingest (metric/value/tags/timestamp shape plus the clock-skew guard, default 300 s). Invalid frames are dropped and counted (invalid in admin stats).
  3. The sink calls store.insert_many once per drained batch inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (series resolution, partition DDL, and the measurement inserts all commit together) — a 1024-point burst costs one commit.

database.batch_size (default 2000) exists in the config and is honored by benchmark/load tooling (scripts/benchmark.py batches via insert_many with --batch). See benchmarks for the numbers.

Query path and the rollup fast path

A query first decides whether the rollup can answer it (see Queries):

  • Eligible: aggregation ∈ {avg, sum, min, max, count}; a whole-hour interval (1h, 2h, 1d, …) or none; a window spanning at least two completed hours; an end hour at or below the rollup watermark (i.e. not in the still-rolling region).
  • Not eligible (falls back to raw rows): first, last, median, p95, p99; non-hour intervals; windows shorter than two hours; or a window whose end hour is beyond the rollup watermark (the in-progress hour's partial data is still read from raw rows and merged).

Eligible queries split the window into three disjoint sources: the first edge hour and the last (partial) hour read from raw rows, the fully-inside hours read from rollup_hourly — then merged per bucket. Nothing is double-counted, and the in-progress hour is always served from raw rows, so rollup results are exact, never approximate. Queries the rollup cannot serve fall back in two tiers: avg/sum/ min/max/count downsamples are grouped per bucket inside SQLite (no rows materialized); only first/ last/median/p95/p99 and gap filling stream raw rows into Python (bounded by query.max_rows). This is what makes wide-window aggregates near-constant cost instead of linear in rows scanned (benchmarked ~11.6× at 20,000 points per series — see benchmarks).

Rollup maintenance

rollup_new_hours aggregates each part of the partition grouped by hour (SUM/Min/Max of count/sum/min/max) and writes into rollup_hourly with INSERT OR REPLACE, so re-runs are idempotent. Progress is tracked by a last_hour watermark in rollup_meta; each pass only scans data accrued since the previous pass. RollupManager runs this in a worker thread every rollup.interval (default 5m), and only rolls hours that are at least reject_client_timestamp_skew_s old — a late write can never land in an already-rolled hour. Assumption: in-order ingestion (enforced by the 300 s clock-skew guard); a backfill into an already-rolled past hour needs a rebuild (replace=True).

Retention

Retention is monthly-granular: RetentionManager (retention.check_interval, default 1h; first pass runs on boot) drops each measurements_YYYY_MM partition whose last day is older than the TTL (retention.default_ttl, default 30d, units s/m/h/ d/w). A drop removes the whole partition table and it also deletes those hours from rollup_hourly (two operations in one pass — a table drop plus a row delete). Deleted data leaves no aggregate trace. Space is reusable incrementally (auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL) plus on demand via sqtseries vacuum.

Background tasks

TaskDefault intervalPurpose
RollupManager5mBuild hourly pre-aggregates of completed hours (raw-read cost amortized)
RetentionManager1hDrop partitions older than the TTL and their rollup rows
MaintenanceManager1hANALYZE planner statistics
CheckpointManager60sTRUNCATE WAL past 64 MB; warn on readers blocking checkpoints

Rollup, retention, maintenance, and backup run in worker threads (asyncio.to_thread); the CheckpointManager issues its short wal_checkpoint PRAGMA directly from the event loop. Rollup and retention start with an immediate first pass instead of waiting out the interval.

SQLite pragmas

PRAGMAValueWhen
journal_modeWALEvery connection
synchronousNORMALEvery connection
page_size8192Once, before tables (fresh file only)
auto_vacuumINCREMENTALOnce, before tables (fresh file only)
cache_size−64000Every connection
mmap_size268435456 (256 MB)Every connection
busy_timeout5000Every connection
temp_storeMEMORYEvery connection
journal_size_limit67108864 (64 MB)Every connection
foreign_keysONEvery connection
threads4Every connection
analysis_limit400Every connection
wal_autocheckpoint0 (readers) / 10000 (writer)Per connection

Reader connections never trigger checkpoints (prevents reader/writer contention); the writer autocheckpoints every 10,000 pages (~80 MB at the configured 8 KiB page size, far above SQLite's 1,000-page default). The CheckpointManager (every 60 s) performs a TRUNCATE checkpoint as soon as the WAL file reaches 64 MB — a reader holding a read lock that blocks TRUNCATE is reported (busy_runs, warning after 3 consecutive blocked runs).

Durability and crash recovery

Writes are crash-atomic: synchronous=NORMAL + WAL means an abrupt SIGKILL loses nothing the process acknowledged. On the next startup the service runs check_integrity_on_startup (quick_check, warn on failure rather than refuse to boot) and then recover_wal (ensures WAL mode + one PASSIVE checkpoint). run_analyze_once runs after all sockets have bound. On shutdown, the service runs run_optimize (PRAGMA optimize) and finishes with a TRUNCATE WAL checkpoint — a clean close with no WAL residue. For the full picture — what to back up, how to restore, and when vacuum actually shrinks the file — see Backup & Restore. Backups via VACUUM INTO are consistent snapshots even while writes are in flight, and are fully restorable (backup_database returns the snapshot path; a name collision within the same second raises BackupExistsError). A BackupManager background task takes one snapshot on startup and then every backup.interval (shared with on-demand backups), skipping a snapshot if one younger than the interval already exists. Every connection is closed per-use; no ResourceWarning/fd leaks are observed across the public API.

Concurrency model

  • Single process, a single asyncio event loop. uvicorn runs in-process on the same loop (no subprocess, no thread pool for HTTP).
  • WorkerPool(size=1) pumps ingress, query broker, and admin broker in each loop iteration; sockets are never shared with other threads.
  • Writers are serialized by SQLite itself: BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock up front, busy_timeout waits for it at the file level. Checkpoints, rollup, retention, and maintenance run in worker threads and use their own short-lived connections.
  • State after boot is recorded in runtime.json next to the database file (PID, live ports, DB path) — used by status, stop, and ports; removed on shutdown.

Error handling

FailureHandling
Invalid ingest frameDropped + counted (invalid in admin stats)
Client timestamp skew > 300 sRejected at the ingress (default window)
Query errorsStructured error reply (INVALID_REQUEST, INVALID_QUERY, INTERNAL_ERROR, …)
SQLITE_BUSYbusy_timeout (5 s) waits on the writer lock
Corruptionquick_check at startup (warn, not fail); full integrity_check on suspicion
Long-running readerCheckpointManager logs a warning after 3 blocked runs
VACUUM while writes are in flightAdmin returns VACUUM_BUSY — stop the service and run sqtseries vacuum

Performance characteristics

Measured numbers live in benchmarks, but read them with the path in mind: the benchmark tool drives the engine (insert_many with executemany batches, default 5,000 rows per call) and reaches ~65K–253K rows/sec; sub-millisecond single-series range queries; near-constant wide-window aggregates via the rollup path. The live service ingest path is one transaction per message, so per-frame steady-state throughput is lower — measure on your own hardware with python3 scripts/benchmark.py.
